title: Surge reservation handoff and billing quarantine workflow
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: Implement a controlled handoff mechanism between short-lived surge reservations and long-running dedicated lanes, plus a billing quarantine workflow that isolates suspected surge-driven overage charges for operator review before they appear on customer invoices.
background: Customers have asked for predictable throughput guarantees while still being able to absorb short spikes. Current surge pools immediately bill overage to tenant accounts which leads to support escalations for transient spikes. We need a safer UX: a reservation handoff that transfers running tokens into a dedicated slot when capacity stabilizes, and a billing quarantine that delays final invoicing for suspected transient overages while automated heuristics and ops review reconcile whether charges should be prorated, credited, or applied.
proposed_solution: 1) Reservation Handoff: add ephemeral reservation tokens issued by surge pools that can be claimed by a tenant's dedicated lanes within a 2-10 minute handoff window. If claimed, the runtime migrates warming KV caches and KV pointers without resetting token state. 2) Billing Quarantine: when surge reservations lead to usage beyond committed capacity, flag those usage buckets as 'quarantined-overage' for 72 hours. During quarantine, automated checks run (spike duration, request hotness, tenant opt-in settings) and an ops UI shows candidate credits. After quarantine either the charge is committed, prorated credits applied, or a manual dispute is created. 3) Operator controls and SLA: expose policies to configure grace-window, quarantine duration, and auto-commit thresholds per customer tier.
decision_log: 2025-11-21: Chose ephemeral reservation tokens rather than sticky VM reallocation to reduce resource churn (decision by infra + runtime leads).
2025-11-22: Quarantine window default set to 72 hours; ops can shorten for enterprise customers. (PM + Support consensus).
2025-11-24: Auto-commit threshold: if spike settles and cumulative excess < 5% of monthly committed capacity, auto-apply 100% credit; otherwise surface for manual review. (Finance + Product).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement tokens and quarantine flag in staging; enable for internal tenants only (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (beta): Expose tenant opt-in setting and operator UI; onboard 10 customers under account manager supervision (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): Enable auto-detection for all surge pools with default quarantine behavior and billing UI links (8 weeks).
Rollback: if latency or error rate on handoff > 0.5% or if invoices are incorrectly labeled, disable handoff and revert to immediate billing path.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: handoff_success_rate < 99.5% triggers P1 pager to runtime team.
Metric: quarantine_auto_commit_rate deviates from historical baseline by > 20% triggers ops review.
Alert: number of manual disputes created per day > 5 for a given customer signals policy tuning needed.
Dashboard: per-tenant quarantine queue with ETA, rationale, and linked PRs/PRDs.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation tokens issued and claimable by dedicated lanes; successful handoff preserves KV cache references in 95% of attempts during canary.
Quarantine flagging path records usage events and prevents immediate invoice finalization for quarantined buckets for the configured window.
Automated heuristics apply credits according to the auto-commit policy and produce an auditable decision record.
Operator UI shows quarantined items, allows commit/prorate/dispute, and links to request traces and cost breakdowns.
No customer-facing SLA regressions: 99.9th percentile latency for requests routed through handoff path remains within existing SLO +/- 10ms.
open_questions: Billing: Should quarantined charges appear as 'provisional' on the billing portal or be hidden until commit? (finance tradeoff: transparency vs. churn).
Quota accounting: How do we surface real-time committed capacity vs. reserved tokens in the console without confusing users?
Security: Are ephemeral tokens susceptible to replay or cross-tenant claim? Need threat model and expiry semantics.
Edge-case: What happens when an in-flight handoff collides with instance termination during preemption? (we may need failover copy of minimal KV metadata).
